deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft (with page numbering 25-27) of Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The page finishes the theorem of Art. 17 (Art. 18 in the printed version) and begins Art. 18 (printed Art. 19), the 'Überschlag' (rough count) of the conditions that determine an analytic function.

(A) End of the theorem (Lehrsatz) of Art. 17.
Setting. T is a surface spread over the z-plane, z = x + iy. If T is multiply connected, it is cut by cross-cuts (Querschnitte) into a simply connected T*. A complex quantity alpha + i beta is given at every point. Its 'defect' integral
Omega(alpha, beta) = ∫_T [(alpha_x - beta_y)^2 + (alpha_y + beta_x)^2] dT
is assumed finite. Omega vanishes exactly when alpha + i beta satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann equations.

Claim. alpha + i beta can always be turned into an analytic function u + iv of z by adding a variable complex quantity (u - alpha) + i(v - beta) with these properties:
1. It is purely imaginary at every boundary point, i.e. u = alpha on the boundary.
2. In the interior of T* it is continuous, or discontinuous only at isolated points (footnote 1), with finite Dirichlet integrals ∫|∇(u - alpha)|^2 dT and ∫|∇(v - beta)|^2 dT.
3. On crossing a cross-cut it jumps by a purely imaginary amount. This jump is constant along the cut from one branch point (or endpoint) to the next.
4. Among these jumps, exactly as many are independent as there are cross-cuts.
The added quantity is unique up to an additive constant in the imaginary part.

Reconstruction of the proof (from Arts. 15-17 on the previous page):
- Art. 15-16. Over all lambda vanishing on the boundary, minimise Omega(alpha + lambda, beta). Note that Omega(alpha + lambda, beta) = Omega(alpha, beta) + 2N(lambda) + ∫|∇lambda|^2 dT. At the minimiser u = alpha + lambda the first variation vanishes:
N = ∫[(u_x - beta_y) lambda_x + (u_y + beta_x) lambda_y] dT = 0 for all admissible lambda.
- Art. 17. Integrate by parts (Art. 7, Green's theorem) with X = u_x - beta_y and Y = u_y + beta_x. The boundary term on dT vanishes because lambda = 0 there. Since lambda is otherwise free, this gives Delta u = 0. It also gives zero flux, ∫(X dx/dp + Y dy/dp) ds = 0, around the boundary of every part of T.
- Hence the line integral sigma = ∫_{O0}^{O} (du/dp - dbeta/ds) ds is path-independent in T*. It is single-valued there and jumps by constants across the cross-cuts.
- Set v = beta + sigma. Then v_x = -u_y and v_y = u_x, so u + iv is analytic in T*.
- The added quantity is (u - alpha) + i sigma:
  - Its real part u - alpha = lambda is 0 on the boundary, so the quantity is purely imaginary there.
  - u is single-valued on T, so only sigma jumps across cuts, and the jumps are imaginary.
  - The jumps (periods of the conjugate) are constant along a cut, because both sides have equal derivative. One jump per cut is independent; jumps on the pieces between branch points are tied together by the zero-flux relations.

Uniqueness (Riemann: 'bedarf keiner Ausführung'). The real part u is a minimiser of Omega, which is a strictly convex quadratic in lambda. Suppose two minimisers differ by mu with mu = 0 on the boundary. Then ∫|∇mu|^2 = 0, so mu is constant, hence 0. Then v is fixed up to a constant by the Cauchy-Riemann equations. (Equivalently: the difference of two solutions is analytic, its real part is single-valued and harmonic and vanishes on the boundary, so it is 0.)

(B) Art. 18. Riemann first says the principles above open a way to study definite functions of a complex variable independently of any analytic expression for them. To orient himself, he estimates how many conditions determine such a function in a given region.

Case: T simply connected, so there are no cuts. The function w = u + iv is determined by:
1. u is prescribed at every boundary point. The data must change by an infinitesimal of the same order under an infinitesimal displacement, i.e. a Lipschitz-type condition. Footnote 2 says this restriction is not essential and only avoids unnecessary discussion.
2. v is prescribed at one point.
3. w is finite and continuous everywhere.
These conditions determine w completely.

Proof (begun here, finished on p. 27):
- Choose alpha + i beta with alpha equal to the boundary data, and with the change of alpha + i beta of the same infinitesimal order as the displacement throughout the surface. Riemann says this 'will always be possible'.
- Then the integrand of Omega is bounded, so Omega is finite.
- The theorem gives u + iv with u = alpha on the boundary. With no cross-cuts there are no jumps.
- v is fixed by its prescribed value at one point.
- Uniqueness follows from the theorem.

This is the Dirichlet problem for the real part of an analytic function, solved through the Dirichlet principle.
errors: No algebraic slips on this page. The logical gap is inherited from Art. 16: the existence of a minimiser of Omega (the Dirichlet principle) is assumed, not proved. Weierstrass criticised this in 1870; it was repaired by Schwarz, Neumann and Hilbert (1899-1904).

'was immer möglich sein wird' (the extension of the boundary data alpha to the interior with finite Dirichlet integral) is asserted without proof. It is true for Lipschitz data on reasonable domains. Riemann's Lipschitz-type restriction in condition 1 is actually what makes it true, since Hadamard (1906) showed merely continuous data may admit no finite-energy extension. Footnote 2's claim that the restriction is inessential is right for the solvability of the Dirichlet problem (Perron/Wiener). It is not right for the variational method as stated.

The uniqueness argument via 'the real part always yields a minimum' is only sketched. It needs the strict convexity of the quadratic functional together with the vanishing boundary condition. This is easy, but omitted.

The statement that exactly as many jump constants are independent as there are cross-cuts is asserted, not derived on this page. It relies on the zero-flux condition at branch points (crossings of cuts).

results.what: Any complex field alpha+i beta with finite Omega can be corrected to an analytic function by adding a quantity that is imaginary on the boundary and has constant imaginary jumps across cross-cuts (number of independent jumps = number of cuts); unique up to an imaginary constant
results.modern_name: Existence/uniqueness of a harmonic function with given boundary values and its multivalued harmonic conjugate (periods); Dirichlet principle / Hodge-type decomposition on a bordered surface
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann, Inaugural dissertation 1851 (Art. 18 of printed version), building on Green, Gauss, Thomson, Dirichlet

results.what: Uniqueness via the minimizing property of the real part
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of minimiser of a strictly convex Dirichlet energy / maximum principle

results.what: Analytic function in a simply connected region uniquely determined by Re w on the boundary (Lipschitz data), Im w at one point, and continuity/finiteness
results.modern_name: Dirichlet problem plus harmonic conjugate (Schwarz problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 dissertation Art. 19; rigorous by Schwarz/Neumann (1870s), Hilbert 1900

results.what: Programme: study functions of a complex variable through determining conditions (boundary data, singularities), independent of analytic expressions; counting of conditions
results.modern_name: Riemann's 'geometric' function theory; boundary value problems, later the Riemann-Hilbert problem (cf. p. 27's general linear boundary conditions)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of Arts. 18-19 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation, with nearly the same content as the printed text. These are among his best-known results (Dirichlet principle, boundary determination of analytic functions). Minor wording differences from print, such as 'bloss imaginär' instead of the mu/nu formulation, are of philological interest only.

transcription_corrections: Condition 2: the word read as 'lückenweise' is uncertain in the image. The printed dissertation has 'nur in einzelnen Punkten unstetig', and footnote 1 confirms the discontinuities are confined to isolated points; the handwriting looks more like 'nur leicht'/'stellenweise'. Flag as uncertain.
'von einem Zweigpunkte zum andern' is plausible (Verzweigungs-/Zweigpunkte = points where cross-cuts meet or end).
In footnote 1, 'innerhalb T*' should read as restricting the discontinuities to isolated points inside T*. The transcription is essentially correct.

Footnote 2: 'die gemachte soll nur für unnöthige Erörterungen abschneiden' should probably read 'soll nur unnöthige Erörterungen abschneiden'. 'für' looks spurious, or is a misreading of a word like 'hier'.
Condition 1 of Art. 18: 'Ortsänderung' is consistent with the image, which may read 'Ortsveränderung' as on p. 27.
